EXPLORATORY MODEL • cancer-specific scenario laboratory v0.1

Compare hypothetical cancer bioelectric states.

Examine how membrane capacitance, ionic conductance, a voltage-dependent potassium gate and TPMET electron flux could change a simulated voltage response. Cancer labels identify questions to investigate, not measured tumour-specific signatures.

Scientific status: All supplied cancer-specific parameter sets are invented demonstration scenarios. They are not derived from tumour measurements, do not establish differences between cancer types and must not be interpreted as clinical or treatment predictions. Edit values only using documented, comparable experiments. Simulations do not include proliferation, apoptosis, TTFields or external field coupling.

1 · Select a scenario

2 · Adjust physical quantities

Conductances in nS, capacitance in pF, voltage in mV, electron flux J in fmol electrons/s/cell. Positive injected current is inward.

3 · Compare electrical responses

Voltage trajectories from a simple dynamic conductance model. A 10 pA current pulse runs from 100 to 300 ms. The fixed reference scenario uses identical stimulus settings.

4 · Define falsifiable experiments

Suggested experimental comparison: select a cancer cell line and matched non-malignant reference, measure whole-cell capacitance and conductance under identical conditions, determine whether an independently measured TPMET flux perturbs membrane voltage, then test a targeted ion-channel inhibitor.

Exports include all values, model version, numerical settings and provenance. This is not experimental validation or immutable preregistration.

Model equations, assumptions and limitations

For the modelled potassium branch, gK(V,t) = gK,max [(1−α)+α n(t)], where dn/dt = [n∞(V)−n]/τgate and n∞(V)=1/[1+exp(−(V−Vhalf)/slope)]. The ordinary membrane equation is C dV/dt = −Σ gᵢ(V,t)(V−Eᵢ)+ITPMET+Iapp, with ITPMET=96.48533212 Jη pA for outward electron transport. An RK4 integrator uses 0.05 ms timesteps by default.

There are no ATP, calcium, mitochondrial, tissue, drug, dynamic TPMET, phenotype or external-field equations. The gating form is generic, not a particular characterised channel. Parameters are illustrative and measured values are needed for each cell line and condition. Comparison against a reference uses a second hypothetical scenario, not a healthy-cell control.

Numerical consistency does not establish biological accuracy. An independent calibration/validation data set and a sensitivity analysis are required before quantitative predictions can be relied on.
